text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in the July 11 edition of several Russian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Systematic shortages of food and fuel are bringing Russia's north to the edge of catastrophe.
- NATO'a eastwards expansion will give a powerful impulse to the struggle for new arms markets.
- President Yeltsin has signed two decrees which are to change the system of state control of the oil business in Russia.
- On a Far Eastern island Russian youth are enthusiastically training to join criminal groups in the region.
- Social benefits paid to various groups of Russian citizens are an enormous burden for the budget.
- Most of the bills vetoed by President Boris Yeltsin either contradict existing laws or represent the interests of narrow lobbying groups, says the president's administration paper.
